transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m constantly losing the tools and paperwork I need at work, and it’s starting to cause real problems on the line. I work at a meat processing plant, and misplacing my equipment is starting to slow down production and get me in trouble with my supervisors.
Have you struggled with losing things and staying organized like this since you were a child, or is this a relatively new change for you?

It's definitely not new; I've struggled with this since I was a kid. Back in primary school, my teachers would write on my report cards that I was always daydreaming, forgetting instructions, and losing my worksheets. But it has really come to a head over the last two years since I started working full-time at the plant and trying to do my certification courses.
Besides your struggles with focus and organization, have you also been experiencing a persistently low mood, or excessive, constant worry about various everyday things?

No, I wouldn't say I have a persistently low mood or constant worry about everyday things. Any stress or frustration I feel is really just tied to my struggles with staying organized and how that's affecting my performance at work.
Do you often feel physically restless, find it hard to sit still, or act on impulse, or would you say your difficulties are almost entirely with focus and organization?

My struggles are definitely almost entirely with focus and organization, not physical restlessness. I don't have any trouble sitting still or acting on impulse; it’s more that my mind constantly drifts off and I can't keep track of my tools or what I'm supposed to be doing.
When you were a child, did you ever have trouble with being overly active, such as constantly running around, climbing on things, or finding it hard to wait your turn?

No, I don't recall ever being overly active, running around, or having trouble waiting my turn when I was a kid. My struggles back then were different, mainly daydreaming, forgetting instructions, and constantly losing my school worksheets. I was always the quiet kid who just spaced out and needed things repeated.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a long-standing history of inattention, disorganization, and forgetfulness dating back to childhood (primary school), which currently causes significant functional impairment at his workplace. He denies any history or current symptoms of hyperactivity or impulsivity. Under ICD-10, Attention Deficit Disorder without hyperactivity is classified under F98.8 (Other specified behavioral and emotional disorders with onset usually occurring in childhood and adolescence).
